name: 深沟潭
Trench Pool
before: 海边礁上一个大潭，潭口通着外海，潭底黑得看不见。每逢大潮，海沟里的大鱼就顺着冷水涌上来，一条比船还长，嘴能吞下一只渔筐，把漂客们下在潭边的鱼簖一道道撞烂。一营守墟人守在潭边，三路排开，谁去修簖就把谁往水里推，像是给大鱼喂食。

A great pool in the reef on the coast, its mouth open to the outer sea, its bottom too black to see. At every spring tide the big fish from the trench come up with the cold water, each longer than a boat, mouths that could swallow a fish basket whole, and they smash the castaways' fish weirs round the pool one after another. A camp of Ruin-keepers holds the pool's edge in three columns, shoving into the water anyone who comes to mend a weir, as if feeding the fish.
after: 守墟人退了，大鱼被你们拿长叉和火把赶回了潭底，鱼簖修了起来。可潭底连着海沟，深不见底，下一回大潮，又会有大鱼顺着冷水上来，守墟人也会回到潭边。漂客们说，清一回，能吃上一个月的安生鱼。阿汐在潭边找到爹的一道刻痕：「大潮勿近此潭。」

The keepers withdraw, you drive the great fish back to the depths with long tridents and torches, and the weirs go up again. But the pool's bottom opens onto the trench and has no end to it: at the next spring tide more great fish will rise with the cold water, and the keepers will return to the edge. Clear it once, the castaways say, and you get a month of fishing in peace. By the pool Axi finds one of her father's marks: 'Keep clear of this pool at spring tides.'

name: 接篙礁
Pole-Passing Reef
before: 野地边一道干礁，礁上拴着一条小领港船，船头插着一根竹篙，篙上刻满了尺寸。一个十七八岁的漂客后生坐在船里，被一队亡骑团团围着，不许他把船推下水。他梗着脖子喊：「我是领港！礁门进船要我领！」亡骑不懂，只管把他的篙一次次拔出来扔掉。

A dry reef at the edge of the open land, a little pilot boat tied up on it with a bamboo pole planted in its bow, the pole notched all over with measurements. A castaway lad of seventeen or eighteen sits in the boat surrounded by a troop of dead riders who won't let him push it into the water. He sticks out his neck and shouts, 'I'm a pilot! Ships coming through the reef gate need me to bring them in!' The riders don't understand; they just keep pulling out his pole and throwing it away.
after: 亡骑散了，后生把篙插回船头。他叫阿礁，是许潮生教出来的，那几年天天跟着他量礁门。往东走那天，许潮生把这根篙交给他：「后头还会有船来，你领它们进来。我女儿要是来了，你不用领，她看潮比我准。」阿礁把篙递给阿汐，她没接：「你领吧，爹说我不用。」

The riders scatter and the lad plants his pole back in the bow. His name is A Jiao. Xu Chaosheng trained him, and in those years he followed him every day to sound the reef gate. The day they went east, Xu gave him this pole. 'More ships will come. You bring them in. If my daughter comes, you needn't guide her; she reads the tide better than I do.' A Jiao looks at Axi and holds out the pole. Axi doesn't take it. 'You keep guiding. Father said I wouldn't need to.'

name: 南屿埠
South Islet Landing
before: 葫芦筏靠上南屿，岸上一道石阶通上屿顶，阶边每隔一百步摆一枚刻了痕的贝壳，跟扫沙道上的一模一样。阶口蹲着一队亡弓，弓已经搭好了箭。哑巴渡夫比画着不肯靠岸，阿汐却已经跳进了齐腰的水里。

The gourd raft touches the South Islet, where a flight of stone steps climbs to the summit with a notched shell set every hundred paces, the same as on the Swept Sand Path. A squad of dead archers crouches at the foot of the steps, arrows already nocked. The mute ferryman gestures that he won't land, but Axi has already jumped into the waist-deep water.
after: 亡弓退了，阿汐顺着贝壳往上走，一步也不停。最后一枚贝壳摆在屿顶的一块平石上，里头盛着一点干了的海盐，像是谁把一捧海水放在这里晒干了。龚墨斗在后头喘着气说：「你爹做事，比账房还讲究。」

The archers withdraw and Axi follows the shells up without stopping once. The last one lies on a flat stone at the top of the islet with a little dried sea salt in it, as if someone had set down a handful of seawater here to dry. Gong Modou, panting behind her, says, 'Your father did things more carefully than a bookkeeper.'

name: 送船石
Seeing-Off Stone
before: 南屿顶上一块大平石，石下一座小屋，屋前晾着网，是屿上几户漂客的仓。一伙落难海盗占了仓，把渔家撵到了石头底下住，仓里的粮他们吃，渔网他们拿去拦海湾收过路钱。平石上刻着字，海盗嫌碍事，拿刀刮去了一半。

On the summit of the South Islet lies a great flat rock with a little hut below it, nets drying out front: the store of the few castaway families on the islet. A band of shipwrecked pirates has taken it, driving the fisherfolk to live under the rock, eating the grain and stringing the nets across the bay to charge passing boats a toll. Words are carved into the flat rock, and the pirates, finding them in the way, have scraped half of them off with knives.
after: 海盗被赶下了屿，渔家搬回了仓。阿汐跪在平石前，把没刮掉的字一个个摸出来：「领港许潮生，送船到此。礁门以内，潮由我领；礁门以东，不用领了。汐，爹往前去了。」她把奶奶那封信压在字底下，压了块石头。起身时，她看见石边的软泥里有一行新脚印，左脚印里带着黄沙，右脚印里带着红泥，往东去了。

The pirates are driven off the islet and the fisherfolk move back into their store. Axi kneels before the flat rock and traces the surviving words one by one: 'Pilot Xu Chaosheng saw the ships this far. Inside the reef gate, the tide was mine to read; east of the reef gate, there is no need of a pilot. Xi, Father has gone on ahead.' She lays her grandmother's letter beneath the words and weighs it down with a stone. As she rises she sees a line of fresh footprints in the soft mud beside the rock, yellow sand in the left prints, red mud in the right, heading east.
first: 仓里抄出海盗囤的两缸番薯干、一筐鸡蛋、八张拦海的大网、一桶收来的过路钱，还有一包从平石上刮下来的石粉，他们留着说要卖给漂客「当符水喝」。

In the store you seize the pirates' hoard: two vats of dried sweet potato, a basket of eggs, eight big nets for blocking the bay, a bucket of toll money, and a packet of stone dust scraped off the flat rock, which they meant to sell to the castaways 'to drink as a charm'.
pass: 每次路过，屿上的渔家都往你们船上搬一篓鱼，再替阿汐在平石前扫一遍落叶：「许先生的字，我们替他看着，你们放心往前走。」

Each time you pass, the islet's fisherfolk carry a basket of fish to your boat and sweep the leaves from before the flat rock for Axi. 'We'll look after Teacher Xu's words for him. You go on ahead and don't worry.'

name: 驮茶栈
Tea Pack Warehouse
before: 大路边一座长长的土栈，是马帮当年存茶的地方，墙上还挂着一排驮架。一伙落难海盗占了土栈，听说里头有「千里号的普洱」，把墙挖了好几个洞，挖出来的茶砖一块块堆在门口，拿来跟漂客换酒。守门的弓手站在驮架上，谁靠近就放箭。

A long earthen warehouse beside the main road where the caravan once stored its tea, a row of pack frames still hanging on its walls. A band of shipwrecked pirates has taken it on hearing there is 'the Qianli's Pu'er' inside, digging several holes through the walls and piling the bricks they found at the door to swap with the castaways for wine. Their archers stand on the pack frames and shoot anyone who comes close.
after: 海盗被赶走，茶砖码回了栈里。看栈的漂客老汉说，马帮走时留下话：「茶是镖，不是货，等镖头来了点验。」可等了十年，茶砖也陈成了老茶，一块比一块香。他拍拍茶堆：「镖头再不来，这茶就成了宝了。」

The pirates are driven off and the bricks are stacked back inside. When the caravan left, says the old castaway who minds the warehouse, they left word: 'This tea is a consignment, not goods for sale. Wait for the chief to come and check it.' Ten years of waiting, and the bricks have aged into old tea, each more fragrant than the last. He pats the pile. 'If the chief doesn't come soon, this lot will be worth a fortune.'
first: 门口抄出海盗换剩的四十块茶砖、六坛酒、一口铁锅、两副驮架，还有一张他们画的「藏宝图」，上面每一个叉都画在茶井上。
At the door you seize what the pirates hadn't traded: forty tea bricks, six jars of wine, an iron pot, two pack frames, and a 'treasure map' they'd drawn, every X on it marked on the tea well.
pass: 每次路过，看栈的老汉都从茶井打一罐水给你们，再掰一角老茶砖塞进罐口：「井水泡老茶，喝了走得动路。镖头的那份我留着。」

Each time you pass, the old warehouseman draws you a jar of water from the tea well and breaks a corner off an old brick to tuck in its mouth. 'Old tea in well water. Drink it and your legs will carry you. I'm keeping the chief's share.'

name: 学水湾
Swimming Lesson Bay
before: 海边一道浅湾，水清得见底，漂客家的孩子们天天在这儿学泅水。今天一队亡弓蹲在湾边的礁上，谁下水就往谁身边射箭，孩子们吓得光着屁股往岸上跑。教泅水的老水手气得直骂：「它们自己不会水，也不许别人会！」

A shallow bay on the coast, its water clear to the bottom, where the castaways' children come every day to learn to swim. Today a squad of dead archers crouches on the reef at the bay's edge shooting arrows beside anyone who enters the water, and the children run for the shore bare-bottomed in fright. The old sailor who teaches them swears in fury. 'They can't swim themselves, so they won't let anyone else!'
after: 亡弓被赶走，孩子们又扑进了水里。老水手说，那几年马帮的汉子也在这湾里学水，山里人一下水就沉，船上的人教了一年。岸边木牌上记着：「老十七，沉。」「老十七，又沉。」「老十七，浮起来了！」最后一行：「镖头也不会水。等他来，再教。」

The archers are driven off and the children plunge back in. In those years, the old sailor says, the caravan men learned to swim in this bay too; mountain men sink the moment they're in the water, and the sailors spent a year teaching them. A wooden board on the shore keeps the record: 'Old Seventeen, sank.' 'Old Seventeen, sank again.' 'Old Seventeen, floated!' The last line: 'The chief can't swim either. We'll teach him when he comes.'

name: 三角旗礁
Pennant Reef
before: 海边一块高礁，礁顶插着一面黑色的三角旗，旗角朝东，归墟没有风，旗却是展开的：旗边缝着竹篾撑着。一队亡弓守在礁下，一箭一箭往旗上射，旗上早已是一片箭孔，就是不倒。

A tall reef on the coast with a black pennant planted on its crest, its point to the east. The Ruins have no wind, yet the pennant stands spread: strips of bamboo are sewn along its edges to hold it out. A squad of dead archers below shoots at it arrow after arrow until it is nothing but arrow holes, and still it does not fall.
after: 亡弓退了。是陆家镖的黑三角旗，旗背面缝着一张油布单子，是镖单：「茶路陆家镖，承运千里号贡茶，自茶山至归墟。」底下一行：「镖已送到，交守灯人点收。」收讫的地方没有签名，只画了一顶小小的斗笠。龚墨斗咂咂嘴：「这收镖的，倒是懒得写字。」

The archers withdraw. It is the black pennant of the Lu family escort, and sewn to its back is an oilcloth slip, a consignment note: 'Lu Family Escort of the tea road, carrying the Qianli's tribute tea from the Tea Mountains to the Ruins.' Below it: 'Consignment delivered, received and checked by the lamp keeper.' Where the receipt should be signed there is no name, only a little drawing of a straw hat. Gong Modou clicks his tongue. 'Whoever took delivery couldn't be bothered to write.'

name: 合砖石
Joining Stone
before: 野地里一块方石，石面上嵌着半块茶砖，茶砖压得紧，十年了一角没缺，另一半的位置空着，正好一个半块的凹槽。头一天还在头骡湾朝西站着的那头老白骡，不知什么时候自己走到了这里，卧在方石边上。一队亡骑围着它，要把它赶走，它头也不抬。

A square stone in the open with half a tea brick set into its face, pressed so tight that in ten years not a corner has crumbled. Where the other half should be there is an empty socket exactly half a brick in size. The old white mule that stood facing west at Lead Mule Bay has somehow walked here on its own and lies down beside the stone. A troop of dead riders surrounds it, trying to drive it off, and it does not even raise its head.
after: 亡骑退了，老白骡还卧着。方石侧面刻着马帮的字：「茶路二百余人，半砖在此；另一半在镖头匣里。两半合上那天，茶路才算到了。」凹槽边磨得发亮，是十年里一只骡子的下巴磨的。小桨蹲下摸了摸骡头：「它不朝西看了。它知道镖头的那一半，要往这边来。」

The riders withdraw; the old mule stays lying there. On the side of the stone the caravan carved: 'Two hundred-odd of the tea road. Half our brick is here; the other half is in the chief's casket. Only the day the halves are joined will the tea road have arrived.' The rim of the socket is worn glossy by ten years of one mule's chin. Xiaojiang crouches and strokes its head. 'It's stopped looking west. It knows the chief's half is coming this way.'

name: 驼铃坑
Camel Bell Pit
before: 野地里一片沙坑，坑口压着几块大石，石缝里露出一截驼鞍的皮带。一队亡弓守在坑边，比别处的都凶，见人就射。打到一半，弓手堆里走出一个亡骑，牵着马，枪头上挂着一枚驼铃。它站到你们和弓手中间，伸手把一张弓按了下去。

A sand pit in the open, its mouth weighed down with boulders, the strap of a camel saddle showing through a crack. A squad of dead archers guards it, fiercer than anywhere else, shooting on sight. Halfway through the fight a dead rider steps out from among the archers leading his horse, a camel bell hanging from his spearhead. He stands between you and the archers and presses one of their bows down with his hand.
after: 是断弦亭网里救出来的那一个。弓手们退了，它搬开坑口的大石，退后一步。坑里埋着几副驼鞍，鞍袋里一本厚账，是驼客留下的「人账」：二百九十九个人，一人一行，生在哪儿、会什么、爱吃什么，都记着。珠珠抱着账本直抖：「我差的人，全在这儿了。」驼铃叮了一声，那个亡骑已经走远了。

It is the one you freed from the net at the Broken String Pavilion. The archers withdraw and he rolls the boulders from the pit's mouth and steps back. Buried inside are several camel saddles, and in a saddlebag a thick ledger the camel folk left behind, a ledger of people: two hundred and ninety-nine of them, one line each, where they were born, what they could do, what they liked to eat. Zhuzhu hugs it with shaking hands. 'All the people I was missing, they're all here.' The camel bell chimes once; the rider is already far away.

name: 跪驼坪
Kneeling Camel Flat
before: 野地里一片平坪，坪上卧着一峰老骆驼，毛掉了大半，两个驼峰软软地塌着，是丝路驼队剩下的最后一峰。一队亡骑围着它，用枪杆捅它起来，它不起，捅一下，哼一声。珠珠一看见它就冲了过去，被一匹灰马挡在了半路。

On a level flat in the open lies an old camel, half its hair gone, both humps sagging soft: the last camel left of the Silk Road caravan. A troop of dead riders surrounds it, prodding it with spear shafts to make it stand. It won't; each prod gets a grunt. Zhuzhu runs at it the moment she sees it and is blocked halfway by a grey horse.
after: 亡骑退了。老骆驼抬起头，看了珠珠很久，慢慢屈下前腿，朝她跪了下来：骆驼只给主家的人跪。驼鞍上拴着一块铜牌：「驼主李二算，妻柳氏。」珠珠在人账里翻到这一行，旁边写着：「女一，名珠算，寄养漂客家。账清即回。」她在两个名字上画了圈，又画了一个小的。

The riders withdraw. The old camel raises its head and looks at Zhuzhu a long while, then slowly folds its forelegs and kneels to her: a camel kneels only to its own household. A brass tag is tied to its saddle: 'Camel master Li Ersuan, and wife, née Liu.' Zhuzhu finds the line in the ledger of people. Beside it is written: 'One daughter, named Abacus Count, left in a castaway family's care. Will return when the accounts are settled.' She draws circles round both names, then draws a small one beside them.

name: 点数滩
Headcount Strand
before: 海边一片长滩，滩头埋着一口大陶缸，缸口用石板盖着，石板上刻着一个大大的「数」字。一队亡骑沿着滩来回跑，谁走近陶缸，就从马上俯身一枪杆把人挑开。漂客们说，那缸是驼客临走那天埋的，谁也不知道里头装的是什么。

A long strand on the coast with a great clay vat buried at its head, its mouth capped with a stone slab carved with one large character: 'Count'. A troop of dead riders gallops back and forth along the beach, leaning down to flick away with a spear shaft anyone who goes near the vat. The camel folk buried it the day they left, the castaways say. No one knows what's inside.
after: 亡骑退了，你们掀开石板，缸里是满满一缸小石子。驼客走之前点了最后一回人，一人往缸里扔一颗。珠珠趴在缸边一颗颗数，数了一下午：石子没有二百九十九颗，缸底留着三个空着的小坑，坑边刻着「待」。人账翻到最后，也有三行只有名字，没有「已往东」。

The riders withdraw and you lift the slab: the vat is full of small pebbles. Before they left, the camel folk counted heads one last time, each dropping a pebble in. Zhuzhu leans over the rim and counts them one by one all afternoon: there are not two hundred and ninety-nine. At the bottom of the vat three small hollows have been left empty, each carved with the word 'Awaiting'. And at the end of the ledger of people, three lines carry only a name and no 'gone east'.

name: 回潮滩
Returning Tide Strand
before: 南边海滩尽头，每回涨潮，静水里就一排排站起守墟人来：亡兵从水底走上滩，亡弓的弓背上挂着海草，亡骑的马蹄底下淌着水。潮涨一回，上来一批，跟漂客们抢滩，抢到哪儿，哪儿的屋子就空了。珠珠抱着人账站在你们身后，一点也不躲。

At the far end of the southern beach, every time the tide comes in, Ruin-keepers stand up out of the still water rank on rank: soldiers walking up the sand from the seabed, seaweed hanging from the archers' bows, water streaming from under the riders' hooves. With each tide a new batch comes up to contest the beach with the castaways, and wherever they take, the houses empty. Zhuzhu stands behind you hugging her ledger of people and does not shrink back at all.
after: 这一潮的守墟人退回了水里，滩上的漂客把屋子收拾了回来。可归墟的潮一天两回，每回都带上来新的，过些日子还得再来清一遍。珠珠坐在滩上，把人账和自己的破账并在一起，一个圈一个圈地对，对完了，账上整整二百九十九个圈。她在最后添了一格，空着，咬着笔头想了半天：「这一格，我算不出来。东边那个点灯的人，大概会算。」

This tide's keepers sink back into the water and the castaways put their houses to rights. But the Ruins have two tides a day, and every one brings new keepers up; before long the beach will need clearing again. Zhuzhu sits on the sand and lays the ledger of people beside her own tattered one, checking circle by circle, and when she is done there are exactly two hundred and ninety-nine. At the end she adds one more box and leaves it empty, chewing her pen a long while. 'I can't work this one out. The man who lights the lamps over east can probably do it.'

name: 藏页营
Torn Page Camp
before: 马蹄印从拆船簿那间木屋一路往山脚去，钻进一道死胡同似的石峡，峡底扎着一营守墟的精兵，三路排开，比外头的都齐整。营当中一座石台，台上压着一块石头，石头底下露出一角纸，被守墟人围得水泄不通。

The hoofprints lead from the hut of the Breaking Ledger to the foot of the hills and into a dead-end stone gorge. At its far end stands a camp of picked Ruin-keepers in three columns, better ordered than any outside. In its centre is a stone platform with a rock weighing something down, a corner of paper showing beneath it, and the keepers are packed so tight around it not a drop could leak through.
after: 精兵退了，石头底下就是撕掉的那半页，许潮生的字：「三号舱失火，大浪将至，鲍老针令众上山。浪后，二至五号尽伤，不能再航；三号灶火烧了半舱；一号随浪而去，不知所终。守墟人在旁看我们锯船，看了十天，也学着锯。众议：船既不能走，拆木分与漂客；人往东行，不用船。」守墟人不懂这页纸，可它们知道这是要紧的东西，就撕下来守着。三个老人的话，各对了一截：船是浪打坏的，火是灶里的，锯子是人拿的，守墟人只是在旁边看。

The picked guards withdraw, and beneath the rock is the torn-out half page in Xu Chaosheng's hand: 'Fire in Three's hold. A great wave coming. Bao Laozhen ordered everyone up the mountain. After the wave, Two to Five all damaged beyond sailing; the cookhouse fire burned half of Three's hold; Number One carried off by the wave, whereabouts unknown. The keepers stood watching us saw up the ships for ten days, and learned to saw too. Agreed by all: since the ships cannot sail, break them and share the timber with the castaways; we go east, and need no ships.' The keepers couldn't read the page, but they knew it mattered, so they tore it out and guarded it. Each of the three elders had a piece of the truth: the wave broke the ships, the fire came from the stove, people held the saws, and the keepers only watched.

name: 解结岬
Untied Knot Point
before: 海边一道石岬，岬尖一根系船柱，柱上缠着一圈圈缆绳，每一圈都打着结，从柱脚一直打到柱顶。一队亡骑守着岬口，绕着石柱跑，跑一圈，马尾巴扫一下缆绳，结越扫越紧。小桨一看见那些结，脸就白了。

A stone point on the coast with a mooring bollard at its tip, wound with turn after turn of rope, each turn knotted, from the foot of the bollard to the top. A troop of dead riders guards the neck of the point, galloping round the bollard, their horses' tails sweeping the rope on every lap until the knots pull tighter and tighter. Xiaojiang goes white the moment he sees them.
after: 亡骑退了，小桨一个个摸那些结：底下全是「等着」，是爷爷来的那几年天天打的。最顶上一个不一样，是活结，一拉就开。小桨拉开它，绳头垂下来，指着东边。「爷爷教过，」他小声说，「『等着』打完了，最后打一个活结，叫『走了』。」

The riders withdraw and Xiaojiang feels the knots one by one. Every one below is a Wait, tied daily through the years Grandpa was here. The topmost is different, a slip knot that opens with a single pull. Xiaojiang pulls it and the rope's end drops loose, pointing east. 'Grandpa taught me,' he says quietly. 'When you're done tying Waits, the last knot you tie is a slip knot. It's called Gone.'

name: 号子营
Rowing Chant Camp
before: 野地里一大营守墟人，三路排开，都坐在地上，一排一排，像坐在船上划桨：手里没有桨，可一齐往前一探，往后一拉，动作整得一丝不差。营里没有声音，只有一个亡兵站在最前头，张着那张没有嘴的脸，像在喊号子。

A great camp of Ruin-keepers in the open, three columns of them sitting on the ground row after row as though seated at the oars of a boat. They hold no oars, yet together they reach forward and pull back in perfect unison. The camp is silent but for one dead soldier standing at the very front, that mouthless face lifted as if calling the stroke.
after: 守墟人退了。小桨站到那个领号子的位置上，想了想，扯开嗓子喊起了爷爷的号子：「一桨听浪呦——二桨听风——三桨不听，往前冲——」营边的漂客们愣了：十年前，他们就是听着这支号子，看千里号的人在这片地上学划桨的。马帮和驼客在这片旱地上学划了一整年。

The keepers withdraw. Xiaojiang takes the caller's place at the front, thinks a moment, and bellows out his grandfather's rowing chant: 'First stroke, hear the waves, oh! Second stroke, hear the wind! Third stroke, hear nothing, and drive on through!' The castaways at the camp's edge stand stunned. Ten years ago, to that very chant, they watched the Qianli's people learn to row on this ground: muleteers and camel men practising for a whole year on dry land.

name: 叩掌屋
Palm-Tapping House
before: 野地里一间小屋，屋里住着个又聋又哑的老阿婆，听不见浪，也说不了话。一队亡兵堵在她门口，不许人进出，她就隔着窗缝伸出一只手，在掌心里拍拍点点，没人看得懂。小桨盯着她的手看了一会儿，忽然挤到最前头：「她在跟我说话。」

A little house in the open where an old woman lives who is deaf and mute, unable to hear the waves or speak. A squad of dead soldiers blocks her door and lets no one in or out, so she pokes one hand out through a crack in the window and taps and dabs at her palm in a way no one can follow. Xiaojiang watches her hand a moment, then shoves his way to the front. 'She's talking to me.'
after: 亡兵被赶走，老阿婆拉着小桨的手，在他掌心里拍。小桨一边看一边念：那几年鲍老针天天来，在她手心里拍给她听海：轻点是浪，重点是风，一下下长的是潮。最后一回，他拍的是「我往东了，耳朵留给你」。她把这几下拍在小桨手心里，拍了三遍，然后拍拍他的头。

The soldiers are driven off and the old woman takes Xiaojiang's hand and taps on his palm. He reads it aloud as she goes: in those years Bao Laozhen came every day and tapped the sea into her palm so she could hear it: light taps for waves, heavy for wind, long slow strokes for the tide. The last time, what he tapped was 'I'm going east. I'm leaving you my ears.' She taps it into Xiaojiang's palm three times, then pats him on the head.

name: 不应崖
No-Answer Cliff
before: 海边一道高崖，崖下就是东边的海。一队亡兵守着崖顶，谁上来就推谁下去。小桨要上崖，说爷爷教的法子得在这儿试一试：冲雾里喊一声，回声快是崖，慢是岛，没有回声，是开阔海。他攥着拳头，咬着嘴唇，等你们把路打开。

A high cliff on the coast with the eastern sea directly below. A squad of dead soldiers holds the top and pushes anyone who climbs up back down. Xiaojiang is determined to go up; there is a trick of Grandpa's he has to try here: shout into the fog, and a quick echo means a cliff, a slow one an island, and no echo at all, open sea. Fists clenched, lip bitten, he waits for you to clear the way.
after: 亡兵退了，小桨站在崖边，冲东边使尽力气喊了一声「爷爷——」。你们一起等着。等了很久，什么也没回来。他回过头，眼睛亮亮的：「没有回声，前头是开阔海。」又低声补了一句：「爷爷没骗我，东边真有路，就是太远了，声音够不着。」

The soldiers withdraw. Xiaojiang stands at the cliff's edge and shouts east with all his strength: 'Grandpa!' You all wait. You wait a long time, and nothing comes back. He turns round, eyes shining. 'No echo. It's open sea ahead.' Then, more quietly: 'Grandpa didn't lie to me. There really is a way east. It's just too far for a voice to reach.'

name: 听潮栈
Tide-Listening Stop
before: 海边一座小栈，屋檐下挂着一排竹筒，竹筒里塞着干草，耳朵贴上去能听见海。这是领港们当年歇脚的地方。一伙落难海盗占了栈，拿竹筒装酒，把漂客赶下了海滩。守门的弓手醉醺醺的，射箭倒是一射一个准。小桨揣着爷爷的竹筒，在栈外站住了。

A small rest stop on the coast with a row of bamboo tubes hanging under its eaves, stuffed with dry grass; press your ear to one and you can hear the sea. Pilots used to rest here. A band of shipwrecked pirates has taken it, using the tubes for wine and driving the castaways off the beach. The archers on the door are reeling drunk but hit whatever they aim at. Xiaojiang, his grandfather's bamboo tube tucked in his shirt, stops outside.
after: 海盗被赶走，竹筒挂回了屋檐。小桨坐在门槛上，终于剥开了爷爷竹筒上的蜡：「小桨：你听得见这几个字，就是到了。爷爷先走一步，前头那条路用不着耳朵，用的是胆子。耳朵借给你，替我听着后来的船。东边有个点灯的，说他会等最后一个人，你去替我谢谢他。」小桨把纸折好，揣回怀里，冲东边的光望了很久。

The pirates are driven off and the tubes go back under the eaves. Xiaojiang sits on the threshold and at last peels the wax from his grandfather's tube. 'Xiaojiang: if you're hearing these words, you've made it. Grandpa has gone on ahead. The road in front needs no ears, only nerve. I'm lending you mine; listen out for the ships that come after. Over east there's a man who lights lamps. He says he'll wait for the last one. Go and thank him for me.' Xiaojiang folds the paper, tucks it back in his shirt, and gazes a long time at the lights to the east.
first: 栈里抄出海盗囤的十二坛酒、一筐干鱼、一捆竹筒、半袋糙米，还有一只铜锣，锣背刻着「千里·四」，被他们拿来当了酒盆。

In the stop you seize the pirates' hoard: twelve jars of wine, a basket of dried fish, a bundle of bamboo tubes, half a sack of coarse rice, and a brass gong engraved 'Qianli Four' on the back, which they had been using as a wine bowl.
pass: 每次路过，栈里的漂客都摘一只竹筒给小桨听一听，再往你们车上搬一筐鱼：「领港的孙子来了，海都安静点。」
Each time you pass, the castaways at the stop take down a bamboo tube for Xiaojiang to listen to and load a basket of fish onto your carts. 'The pilot's grandson is here. Even the sea keeps quieter.'

name: 夜光滩
Glowing Strand
before: 海边一片礁坪，退潮后水只没到脚踝。夜里一脚踩下去，水里就亮起一片蓝光，一步一个亮脚印，一会儿才暗下去。一队亡骑每夜在礁坪上跑，马蹄踏出一溜溜蓝火，把来看光的漂客赶得远远的。礁坪的尽头，一直伸向东边的黑暗。

A reef flat on the coast where at low tide the water only reaches your ankles. At night, every step you take lights the water with a blue glow, one shining footprint after another that only slowly fades. A troop of dead riders gallops across the flat every night, their hooves striking trails of blue fire, chasing off the castaways who come to see the light. At its far end the flat runs on into the darkness of the east.
after: 亡骑散了。墨三说，这光是水里极小的活物，碰一下就亮一下，不是鬼火。看光的老漂客说，千里号的人就是从这里走的：那夜大退潮，几百个人赤着脚踩着礁坪往东走，一人身后一串蓝脚印，几百串，亮了一整夜，天亮才灭。「我活了这么大，」他说，「没见过那么好看的路。」

The riders scatter. The light comes from tiny living things in the water that glow when touched, Mo San says; it is no ghost fire. The Qianli's people left from here, says the old castaway who comes to watch: that night the tide went far out, and a few hundred people walked barefoot east across the reef flat, a trail of blue footprints behind each of them, hundreds of trails, glowing all night and only going out at dawn. 'In all my life,' he says, 'I never saw a road so beautiful.'

name: 东礁门
East Reef Gate
before: 礁坪的尽头，两道黑礁像两扇门，门外的海终于在动：一道道浪从东边涌过来，拍在礁上，碎成白沫，是你们进归墟以来头一回听见浪声。门里扎着守墟人最精的一营，三路排开，背对着浪，面朝着你们，一步也不让。

At the end of the reef flat two black reefs stand like a pair of gates, and beyond them the sea is moving at last: wave after wave rolls in from the east and breaks on the reef in white foam, the first sound of surf you have heard since entering the Ruins. Inside the gate stands the keepers' finest camp in three columns, backs to the waves, faces to you, not yielding a step.
after: 精兵退了，却没有退进水里，而是排在礁门两边，像两排门柱。礁上刻着一行古字：「出此门者，不在海图。」底下有一行新的，刀口还白：「千里号，往东。」沈渡把海图摊在礁上，她的图画到这道门就断了，往东是一片白纸。她把图卷了起来：「以后再说，先把账对完。」

The picked guards withdraw, but not into the water: they form up on either side of the reef gate like two rows of gateposts. An ancient line is carved into the rock: 'Who passes this gate is on no chart.' Below it is a newer one, the cut still pale: 'The Qianli, going east.' Shen Du unrolls her chart on the reef. It stops at this gate; east of it is blank paper. She looks at it a long time, then rolls it up. 'Later. First we finish settling the accounts.'

name: 长席坡
Long Table Slope
before: 野地里一道缓坡，坡上摆着一条长长的席，石头当桌，椰壳当碗，从坡顶一直摆到坡脚，几百个座。一队亡兵一个挨一个坐在席上，面前摆着空碗，坐得端端正正，谁来收碗就把谁按回去。坡边一个老漂客说，这席是给千里号送行摆的，十年没人敢收。

A gentle slope in the open with a long feast laid out down it, stones for tables and coconut shells for bowls, from the top of the slope to the bottom, several hundred places. A squad of dead soldiers sits along it shoulder to shoulder, an empty bowl before each, sitting very properly, and pushes back down anyone who comes to clear the bowls. This feast was laid to see the Qianli off, says an old castaway at the slope's edge. In ten years nobody has dared clear it.
after: 亡兵起身走了，席上空了下来。老人领你们走到坡顶的头一个座：别的碗都倒扣着，表示吃完了；只有这一只是正放着的，碗里一双筷子，搁得整整齐齐，旁边摆着一块干了十年的饼。「老鼎说的，」老人说，「晚到的那个人，回来总得有口热的。」

The soldiers rise and leave and the feast stands empty. The old man leads you to the first place at the top of the slope. Every other bowl lies upside down, to show it was finished; this one alone sits upright, a pair of chopsticks laid neatly across it and beside it a flatbread ten years dry. 'Old Ding's idea,' the old man says. 'Whoever comes late ought to find something hot when he gets here.'

name: 留粮窖
Left Grain Cellar
before: 野地里一座地窖，窖门上刻着「千里号留，后来者取」。一伙落难海盗撬开了窖门，把窖里的粮一袋袋往外搬，搬到海边，要堆成一座小山跟守墟人「买路」出归墟。守窖的是几个漂客，被捆在窖口的木桩上，眼看着粮一袋袋没了。

A cellar in the open, its door carved 'Left by the Qianli, for those who come after.' A band of shipwrecked pirates has prised it open and is hauling out the grain sack by sack, carrying it to the shore to pile into a heap and 'buy passage' out of the Ruins from the keepers. The cellar's guardians, a few castaways, are tied to posts at its mouth, watching the grain disappear sack after sack.
after: 海盗被赶走，粮一袋袋扛回了窖里。守窖的漂客解开绳子，揉着手腕笑：守墟人不收粮，也不卖路，海盗堆了三天，没一个人理他们。窖底码着的粮袋上，每一袋都写着一个名字，是千里号的人一人留了一袋：「我们往前走，吃不着了。」

The pirates are driven off and the grain is carried back down sack by sack. The cellar's guardians untie themselves and rub their wrists, laughing: the keepers neither take grain nor sell passage, and for three days the pirates piled it up with no one paying them any heed. Every sack stacked at the cellar's bottom has a name on it; each of the Qianli's people left one. 'We're going on ahead. We won't need to eat it.'
first: 海边抄回海盗堆的六十袋粮、两口锅、一架从别处抢来的风车，还有一面写着「买路」的白旗，旗杆是一根船桨。
From the shore you recover the pirates' pile: sixty sacks of grain, two pots, a winnowing fan stolen from somewhere, and a white flag reading 'Buying Passage' whose staff is an oar.
pass: 每次路过，守窖的漂客都按千里号的规矩，从写着名字的粮袋里各舀一捧给你们：「这一捧是老鼎的，这一捧是柳娘子的，他们说了，给后来的人。」

Each time you pass, the cellar's guardians follow the Qianli's rule and scoop you a handful from each named sack. 'This handful's Old Ding's, this one's Doctor Liu's. They said it was for whoever came after.'

name: 后来者号
The Latecomer Store
before: 海边最后一片滩上，一座竹棚挑着一面大旗，旗上三个字：「后来者」。棚主是个油头粉面的漂客商人，逢人就说自己就是名单上的第三百个，「最后一行写的就是我」，一张「后来者凭据」卖十文，买了的人死后能进东边的灯里。一队亡骑守在棚前，他说那是他的护卫，其实亡骑只是嫌那面旗晃眼。

On the last beach on the coast a bamboo stall flies a great banner reading 'The Latecomer'. Its owner, a castaway merchant with oiled hair and a powdered face, tells everyone he meets that he is the three hundredth name on the list: 'That last line, it's me.' He sells 'Latecomer certificates' at ten coppers each, which supposedly get you into the lamps over east when you die. A troop of dead riders stands before the stall. His bodyguards, he says; in fact the riders just can't stand how the banner glares.
after: 亡骑退了，棚主见你们桅上的三百盏灯笼，腿先软了，扑通坐在凭据堆上，老实招了：名单他没见过，是听漂客们传的。他佩服你们，把压箱底的好货拿出来跟你们换，换完了，自己动手把那面大旗卷了起来，双手递给你们：「这旗我挂了三年，没一个人信。你们挂，大概有人信。」

The riders withdraw, and when the stallholder sees the three hundred lanterns on your masts his legs give way and he plumps down on his pile of certificates and owns up: he's never seen the list, only heard the castaways talk of it. Impressed with you, he brings out his best goods from the bottom of his chests to trade, and when the trading is done he rolls up the great banner himself and hands it to you with both hands. 'Three years I've flown this and not one person believed me. If you fly it, maybe someone will.'

name: 二百九十九灯
Two Hundred and Ninety-Nine Lamps
before: 灯阵当中，戴斗笠的人放下竹签，转过身，掀开斗笠：瘦脸，花白胡子，左脚草鞋糊着黄沙，右脚糊着红泥，是挂袋树下等你们够信袋的晏伯。他笑了笑：「不急，我晚惯了。」身后二百九十九盏灯一齐亮了一分，静水里一排排站起亡兵、亡弓、亡骑。「十年前三路分手，我替他们来回送信，哪一路点人都差我一个。等我追到归墟，他们已经往东去了，名单留给了守灯的人，就是我。」他从怀里掏出半张名单：「名单上最后一行，要有人填。打得过我，才轮得到你们。」

In the middle of the lamps, the figure in the straw hat lays down his pick, turns, and lifts his hat: a thin face, a grizzled beard, yellow sand on the left sandal and red mud on the right. It is Old Yan, who sat under the Satchel Tree waiting for you to fetch down his bag. He smiles. 'No rush. I'm used to being late.' Behind him all two hundred and ninety-nine lamps brighten a shade, and out of the still water stand rank on rank of dead soldiers, archers and riders. 'Ten years ago the three roads parted, and I ran their letters back and forth between them. Whichever road counted heads, they came up one short: me. By the time I caught up at the Ruins they had gone east, and left the list with the lamp keeper. That's me.' He draws half a name list from his shirt. 'The last line on the list needs someone to fill it. Beat me, and it's your turn.'
after: 守墟人退回了静水。晏伯坐回矮桌，把他的半张和陆九匣里的半张并在一起：二百九十九个手印，最后一行空着，旁边两个小字：「后来者」。「那一行本来留给我，我没赶上，不配写。」你们提笔写下了开拓队的名号。沈渡翻开千里号的日志，在最后一页写：「千里号，到了。」灯里有两盏的灯芯一直没烧短，一盏座上刻着算盘，一盏刻着锁。晏伯指指它们：「这两位，还在路上。」他戴上斗笠，往东礁门走去：「顺路，我先走一步。」

The keepers sink back into the still water. Old Yan sits down at his low table again and lays his half of the list beside the half from Lu Jiu's casket: two hundred and ninety-nine handprints, and the last line blank, two small words beside it: 'Whoever comes after'. 'That line was kept for me. I never caught up, so I've no right to write in it.' You take up the brush and write your company's name. Shen Du opens the Qianli's log and writes on its last page: 'The Qianli has arrived.' Among the lamps, two wicks have never burned down: one stands on a base carved with an abacus, one on a base carved with a lock. Old Yan points to them. 'Those two are still on the road.' He puts his hat back on and walks off towards the East Reef Gate. 'It's on my way. I'll go on ahead.'
